To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the resampling method can be used to create a set of climate scenarios for the Dutch climate that is representative for a large part of the CMIP3 and CMIP5 spread in seasonal temperature changes and (ii) that the resampling method preserves the physical consistencies of the climate model output.

resampling can be used as a tool to create scenarios that preserve the physical consistency of climate models, and that it can be applied to create climate scenarios for climate change adaptation studies in the Netherlands.

the new method for preparing the climate scenarios for adaptation in the Netherlands preserves nearly all physical consistencies as they appear in the model simulations and that the scenarios are based on an ensemble of simulations with the global and regional climate model EC-Earth/Racmo2.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following two issues: (i) the preparation of climate scenarios for the Dutch situation based on a limited number of global simulations and (ii) the development of a method to preserve as much as possible the physical consistencies in the model output when resampling the model output.
the development of a methodology to prepare a set (ensemble) of climate scenarios that are consistent with the CMIP5 ensemble.
developing a method for producing climate change scenarios that are consistent with the CMIP5 ensemble, while preserving the physical inter-variable consistences in the original model simulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scenarios are useful for general applications in climate change adaptation, but that they should not be used for more detailed studies, such as the design of climate change adaptation measures.
the scenarios presented here are a significant improvement over the 2006 scenarios, but they are not yet the best that can be done.
the scenarios are a good basis for climate change adaptation studies in the Netherlands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the resampling of the EC-Earth/ RACMO2 output is an effective way to prepare a set with four scenarios for climate change that can be used in climate change adaptation.
we have developed a method that is able to produce scenarios with a realistic spread of seasonal changes in the Netherlands that are consistent with the CMIP5 results.
the resampling of climate models is a promising method to construct climate scenarios that are consistent in both space and climate variables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
resampling can be a useful tool for preparing climate scenarios.
the resampling method can be used to prepare scenarios for a region that represent a substantial part of the spread in CMIP5.
the use of resampling of model output is a viable alternative for the use of bias-corrected model output in the preparation of climate scenarios.
